Camry Hunt Board

The main hunt, paused on purpose while the market resets.

The target

  • Used Toyota Camry Hybrid — XLE or XSE trim only
  • Front-wheel drive only
  • 30,000 miles or fewer
  • Under $30,000
  • Light color — not black, not white
  • No red interior
  • No glass / panoramic roof
  • 45+ mpg combined (FWD XLE/XSE: 47 mpg ✓)
Also watching: Honda Accord Hybrid EX-L — the Honda comparable to the Camry XLE/XSE, on the same terms. It's the one Accord trim with leather, the 12.3″ screen, and 48 mpg combined.

Status

Waiting for the 2027 Camry to reach Florida lots — expected late Oct to early Nov 2026 — so used prices on 2025/26 cars soften.

Next re-scan: Oct 26, 2026 (early check) — full re-scan Nov 4.

Qualifying Camry matches right now: none. The XLEs found so far were black or white, or priced over budget. It's a patience problem, not a price problem — two ~21k-mile XLEs have already listed under $28k in the wrong colors.

Stock photo: 2025 Camry Hybrid. Silver and light greys are the colors we're waiting on.

Lexus deal watch

An eye stays on the ES 300h the whole time. A genuine standout gets flagged immediately: a Florida car at roughly $42,000 or under, or a sharp price drop on any of the shortlisted cars. The everyday $45–51k listings don't count.

Fuel Math

Based on your driving — about 16,000 miles a year — and gas at $3.90/gallon. Every car in this table is a hybrid. The Camry and the Lexus carry a 13.2-gallon tank; the Accord Hybrid's is a touch smaller at 12.8.

CarGallons / yearFuel cost / yearMiles per tank
Camry LE51 mpg ~314 gal ~$1,224 ~673 mi
Accord Hybrid EX-L48 mpg ~333 gal ~$1,300 ~614 mi
Camry XLE / XSE47 mpg ~340 gal ~$1,328 ~620 mi
Lexus ES 300h44 mpg ~364 gal ~$1,418 ~581 mi

The takeaway: at 16,000 miles a year, the LE's fuel edge over the XLE/XSE is about $104 a year — under nine bucks a month for giving up the leather and the big screen. The Accord Hybrid EX-L slots in just ahead of the Camry XLE/XSE (48 mpg to 47, about $28 a year cheaper) and still runs ~614 miles on a tank despite the smaller tank. The Lexus ES 300h costs about $90 a year more than the XLE/XSE at the pump; the real gap is the sticker, not the gas.

Results as of Oct 21, 2026. Listings change fast — confirm a car is still on the lot before driving to see it.
